# ServicePolicy

ServicePolicy is a Ziti service policy: it lets identities dial or host services, and may require that their devices pass posture checks.

| | |
|---|---|
| API version | `ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Namespaced |
| In Ziti | service policy, `/edge/management/v1/service-policies` |
| Updated with | `PATCH`: a setting that is left out of the spec is left alone in Ziti |

## Example

From [`examples/servicepolicy/servicepolicy.yaml`](../../examples/servicepolicy/servicepolicy.yaml):

```yaml
apiVersion: ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: ServicePolicy
metadata:
  name: web-service-bind
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    kind: ProviderConfig
    name: default
  forProvider:
    name: web-service-bind
    type: Bind
    semantic: AnyOf
    serviceRoles:
      - "#role:web"
    identityRoles:
      - "@web-server"
```

More manifests of the kind: [`examples/scenarios/publish-service.yaml`](../../examples/scenarios/publish-service.yaml).

## Settings: `spec.forProvider`

| Field | Type | Default | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|------|---------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | string, required |  | `name` | Name of the policy. |
| `type` | string, required |  | `type` | Type says what the policy grants: Dial lets the identities connect to the services, Bind lets them host the services. One of `Dial`, `Bind`. |
| `identityRoles` | list of strings |  | `identityRoles`; `@name` is sent as `@id` | IdentityRoles is a list of identity role selectors: "#all", "#attribute" or "@name", where name is the name or the ID of an identity. Names are resolved to IDs. |
| `postureCheckRoles` | list of strings |  | `postureCheckRoles`; `@name` is sent as `@id` | PostureCheckRoles is a list of posture check role selectors: "#all", "#attribute" or "@name", where name is the name or the ID of a posture check. Names are resolved to IDs. |
| `semantic` | string | `AllOf` | `semantic` | Semantic says how the "#attribute" selectors of one list combine: AnyOf selects what has any of the attributes, AllOf what has all of them. One of `AnyOf`, `AllOf`. |
| `serviceRoles` | list of strings |  | `serviceRoles`; `@name` is sent as `@id` | ServiceRoles is a list of service role selectors: "#all", "#attribute" or "@name", where name is the name or the ID of a service. Names are resolved to IDs. |
| `tags` | map of strings |  | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

The settings every managed resource has, such as `spec.providerConfigRef`,
`spec.managementPolicies` and `spec.writeConnectionSecretToRef`, are described
in [Concepts](../concepts.md).

| `serviceRoles` | list of strings | As Ziti reports it. |

| `updatedAt` | string | As Ziti reports it. |

## How it behaves

- Roles are `#attribute`, `#all` or `@name`. A name is looked up in Ziti and sent as `@id`; an ID is accepted as well. Ziti stores IDs, so `status.atProvider` shows `@id`.
- When an entity a role names is deleted in Ziti, Ziti takes the role out of the policy. The provider puts it back once an entity with that name exists again, with its new ID.
- A role that names something that does not exist yet is reported in `Synced` and retried, so policies can be applied together with what they refer to.
- `semantic` says how the `#attribute` roles of one list combine.
- Roles are compared as sets: their order and duplicates do not matter.

## When something goes wrong

- `no entity named "..." in ...` in `Synced`: an `@name` role matches nothing in Ziti yet.
- The policy is ready but the identity still cannot dial: check that the identity and the service share an edge router through an [`EdgeRouterPolicy`](edgerouterpolicy.md) and a [`ServiceEdgeRouterPolicy`](serviceedgerouterpolicy.md), and that the identity passes the posture checks in `postureCheckRoles`.

Create, update, drift, deletion in Ziti and deletion of the resource are covered by the end-to-end test, see [Testing](../testing.md).
